title: Do not dare buy this garbage.
review_text:
I didn't pay for it (and thank God) since I managed to get a free month due to an external subscription, and I thought to try it out a bit for the most mundane things ever.

It couldn't have gone worse.

For starters, I had a manual for how to play a game in Turkish, Italian, and Portuguese for some reason, and I spoke none of those languages, so I decided to upload the PDF to get a translation, only to get sent the message "I cannot translate copyrighted material", which is wild considering this was a manual about how to play something, that came with a game. It's my property, and it's for personal use.

Then, I wanted to try out the image generation tool for changing hairstyles, making the hair longer or shorter, adding some tones of makeup, etc. After barely 15 uploads I started getting the message "image generation is not available in your region", even though it was when I used it seconds before. Next day, same message. It took a month to restart. Of course, it said I had still 35 uploads remaining, so that was bait from the developers for you to think you are getting more than you actually paid for.

Ironically enough, your super mart AI chatbots go to websites and scrape the heck out of them infringing copyright terms every search, as well as pirated game and book sites just to get the information needed to answer the person on the other side, yet it will shout at you every time you need a translation of something you own for personal use, or whenever it feels like it doesn't want to generate more images for you.

Utterly disgusting app, I hope it goes bankrupt soon.

review_text:
I hate the manipulative changes Perplexity has made. The app has been getting worse.

When I use it on my Mac, after connecting my Notion, it says the process doesn’t work. But if I do the exact same thing from my iPad, it works. This never used to happen.

Also, on the computer, when I want to search for something, it didn’t used to automatically select the Computer configuration by default. Now, whenever I search, it’s set to Computer, and when I click Search, it tells me I have to reload something I don’t need, but they’re forcing me to do. It also disables the models I’ve selected for my queries.

Before, I could view Spaces like folders, which was much more visual and easier to understand. As someone with ADHD, that helped me a lot. Now they’ve turned everything into chaotic lists, and over the past few months, Perplexity has ruined the app across all devices.

title: Scam
review_text:
When I signed up, I figured it was a good app to use for light work with contracts and research. Everything was great at first until it was noted that I was using it a lot. Once I began getting comfortable with its functionality, it began to ask for more money for credits outside of the monthly subscription I’m already paying. “Credit’s” is what it was calling it. I fell for it a couple times but began noticing it was when I needed Information on my phone. This was one of a few issues. During the few months I was using it, I had to corrects the math it was doing for me due to the calculations being incorrect and the math wasn’t adding up correctly. I corrected it and received the common answer we’ve all come to get… “ your right to be frustrated “ or “ I see where I went wrong and will correct it”. At this point I would think that simple calculations could be done as it’s nothing more than asking it to do what a calculator does, but it messed up the math I was having it do, consistently. The other issue I have with it is its memory. I would have it write a contract with specific header info and tell it to remember it as we will be using it as a template to go by. It confirmed this request but could NEVER get it correct! 
All in all, if you expect to pay for an AI assistant and get what it tells you in the advertisement, you will be disappointed. It will give you simple answers or information you ask for, but outside of it being a simple search engine… don’t expect much. 
If you try and discuss these concerns with customer service, expect it to be just as frustrating as not getting the product you’ve paid for because that’s what you get. Disappointment and frustration! All in all, 1 star seems too high but it won’t let me give the half star it deserves!

title: Computer changed the game
review_text:
Hands down, this is the best AI app I have ever used. It has completely changed the way I work and has helped me build products that I never would have been able to create on my own. The results have been incredibly valuable, and the platform consistently delivers.

My only real criticism is that I wish Perplexity did a better job of helping users understand how credits and tokens work. While building my last few projects, I ended up using significantly more credits than I expected, which made the overall cost much higher than I had anticipated. The value is absolutely there, but more transparency around token usage and estimated costs would make the experience much better for users.

I would also love to see Perplexity offer a discounted plan or token program for veterans. It would be a meaningful way to support those who are using the platform to build businesses, learn new skills, and create new opportunities after military service.

Overall, despite my concerns about token transparency and pricing, I still believe Perplexity is the best AI platform available today, and I highly recommend it.

Also, I’m not sure that you get as much usage per token as you would using those models natively or whether you have as much control over how those models are configured. But it also has its own native model and even the prior gen of models are so powerful, it shouldn’t be an issue except for very specific use cases.

It’s also been great for the school that I’m doing and kind of acting as like a tutor love how you could tweak what it goals are in certain things however it almost over commits to whatever you tell it to do in like certain projects you have set up. title: Critical Review of Perplexity (Desktop & Mobile)
review_text:
I’ve been using Perplexity across desktop and mobile for quite some time, and unfortunately the experience has been getting worse rather than better. The most frustrating issue is the broken integration of local MCP servers in the desktop app. For several versions now, Perplexity simply no longer connects to local MCP servers reliably, making previously functional workflows unusable. This isn’t just my experience—other users report that all MCP tools became non‑functional after recent updates, including basic commands like ls /tmp or reading local files, with no workaround available.  perplexity.ai

On mobile, the situation isn’t much better. CarPlay support is effectively broken: background noise in the car is constantly misinterpreted as speech input, leading to chaotic or nonsensical interactions. In practice, this makes the app unusable while driving.

Beyond my own issues, many users have voiced additional concerns:

1. MCP Instability, Context Bloat & Security Concerns

Perplexity’s shift away from MCP has left many users confused and frustrated. MCP servers now frequently fail, consume massive amounts of tokens, and introduce reliability issues. Reports show that MCP tool definitions alone can consume tens of thousands of tokens, sometimes up to 72% of the model’s context window, making complex queries nearly impossible.  chatfores... +1
There have also been over 40 documented CVEs related to MCP implementations, raising serious security concerns.  klifehack.com

2. Unresponsive or Ineffective Customer Support

A recurring complaint is that Perplexity’s customer support feels like a “ghost town.” Users report slow or nonexistent responses, even for paid tiers.  Trustpilot

3. Subscription & Credit System Issues

Many reviewers mention unexpected auto‑renewals, hidden credit limits, and sudden fee increases. Some users discovered that features advertised publicly were actually locked behind the highest subscription tier, with no clear disclosure beforehand. Others saw credits disappear after only a few simple queries.  Trustpilot

4. Arbitrary Feature Limitations

Users have reported sudden restrictions on photo uploads—sometimes 10 per day, then suddenly only one—with no warning or explanation.  Trustpilot

5. Reliability Problems After Updates

Recent desktop updates have broken previously stable workflows, especially those relying on MCP tools. Even after restarting, reinstalling, or resetting Spaces, all MCP connectors remain unusable, blocking automation-heavy setups.  perplexity.ai

Overall Verdict

Perplexity used to be a powerful and reliable research assistant, but recent changes have severely degraded the experience. The broken MCP integration, unusable CarPlay voice input, opaque subscription practices, and unreliable updates make it hard to recommend at this point. Unless the company addresses these issues (especially the MCP regression and mobile voice problems) Perplexity risks losing the trust of its most dedicated users.

title: Critiques publiques rédigées par d'autres IA
review_text:
Problèmes de transparence et de gestion
· Restrictions sur les comptes Pro : Les comptes Pro obtenus via offres promotionnelles (ex: Bouygues) sont sévèrement bridés sur les modèles avancés (Gemini 3.1 Pro), parfois après seulement 3 à 5 requêtes, ou 2 envois de documents par semaine. Cela pousse certains vers la formule "Max" à 2000$/an.
· Mode Incognito trompeur : Visé par une action collective, Perplexity est accusé de partager les conversations (même en mode privé) avec Google et Meta via des trackers publicitaires, sans en informer clairement les utilisateurs.

Conflits juridiques et éthiques
· Pillage de contenu : De nombreux éditeurs (New York Times, Reddit, Dow Jones) accusent Perplexity de reproduire intégralement leurs articles, y compris en contournant les paywalls avec son navigateur Comet.
· Non-respect du robots.txt : Accusé d'utiliser des adresses IP non déclarées pour scraper des sites ayant interdit le scraping, ce qui a déclenché plusieurs poursuites.

Modèle économique et viabilité
· Service dévalorisé : Les innombrables offres promotionnelles Pro ont dévalorisé le service. "Donner" l'accès à la moitié d'Internet détériore la qualité pour tous, et peine à convertir les utilisateurs gratuits en payants.
· Perte de parts de marché : Malgré une valorisation élevée, le trafic de Perplexity ne représente que 1,3 % du trafic mondial des chatbots IA (vs 53,9% pour ChatGPT et 27,9% pour Gemini), perdant du terrain face à ses concurrents.

title: Perplexity Pro : Une arnaque juridiquement habillée
review_text:
Si je devais qualifier Perplexity Pro en un seul terme, ce serait : un piège à abonnés. Cette application est conçue avec une malveillance technique rare pilotée par IA, où la transparence est sacrifiée au profit d’une consommation forcée de votre forfait.

Les faits sont pourtant clairs et accablants. Mon abonnement est payé le 20 du mois, consommé le 5 du mois suivant, sans que j’aie fait le moindre excès. Mais ce n’est que la partie émergée de l’iceberg. La fourberie est bien plus profonde : je n’utilise pas la fonction "Pro Search", mais l’application lance ses propres recherches pro à ma place, sans mon consentement. Je n’utilise pas non plus l’option "Computer", mais celle-ci se lance par défaut et consomme mon forfait à mon insu.

C’est une stratégie délibérée : tout, absolument tout, dans cette application est fait pour consommer votre forfait sans votre accord. Les paramètres sont truqués pour vous voler vos crédits, transformant chaque requête banale en une ponction sur votre quota.

Le résultat est sans appel : Perplexity Pro n’est qu’un échantillon payant – une version de démonstration facturée au prix fort, où vous payez pour être dépouillé de vos droits d’utilisation. Ma mise en garde est définitive : réfléchissez très sérieusement avant de payer votre abonnement, car vous ne souscrivez pas à un outil, vous signez un chèque en blanc pour une machine à grignoter vos ressources.

---

Perplexity Pro: A Predatory Subscription Trap

If I had to define Perplexity Pro in a single word, it would be: a legalized scam. This application is engineered with a deeply cynical lack of transparency, designed to forcibly drain your plan without your knowledge.

The facts are damning. My subscription is billed on the 20th of the month, yet my counters are reset to zero on the 5th of the following month, despite me making absolutely no excessive use. However, that is just the tip of the iceberg. The true deceit lies deeper: I do not use the "Pro Search" feature, yet the application launches its own Pro searches on my behalf, without my consent. Likewise, I do not use the "Computer" feature, but it defaults to launching automatically, consuming my plan right under my nose.

This is a deliberate strategy: everything, every single line of code in this app, is deliberately designed to consume your allowance without your approval. The settings are rigged to steal your credits, turning every mundane query into a deduction from your quota.

The conclusion is brutal and irrefutable: Perplexity Pro is nothing more than a paid sample – a trial version you are extorted to pay for, where you fund the very system that robs you. My warning is absolute: think long and hard before you pay for this subscription, because you are not buying a service; you are signing up for a gluttonous mechanism that devours your usage rights without asking for permission.

My breaking point was when I was troubleshooting my desktop PC hardware issues, and I saw perplexity doing searches on macos. When I stopped it and tried to clarify, it fully denied doing so, and doubled down. When presented with the evidence from its logs, it finally admitted to lying. So, it was either a) completely unable to correctly self-assess, or b) it was choosing to withhold that information and lie about it continually. I was honestly really surprised at how unintelligent perplexity seems to be. It struggles with what should be extremely simple prompts. Couple that with the insidious and continuous dishonesty, and I could not allow it to stay on my phone. I hope you don’t allow it to be on yours either.
